sentences.text: Shri Basavaraj R.Math, learned counsel for appellants submitted that appeal was by claimants for enhancement and against dismissal of claim petition against insurer.

3. It was submitted that as per claimants, on 21.03.2010, at about 5.30 p.m. Waman @ Umakanth was traveling in auto rickshaw to go home in Yadgiri, when tractor bearing registration no.KA-33/T-6742 and 6743 driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner dashed against auto rickshaw.

In said accident, Waman @ Umakanth suffered grievous injuries and taken to hospital,
but died during treatment.
Claiming compensation, petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act ('MV Act' for short) was filed against owner and insurer of tractor.
4. Despite service of notice, owner did not appear.
He was placed ex-parte.
Only insurer opposed claim petition denying accident and negligence.
Counter negligence against driver of auto rickshaw was alleged.
It was also contended that driver of auto rickshaw was NC: 2023:KHC-K:7369 charge-sheeted for offences under Sections 3, 181 and 187 of Motor Vehicles Act.
Even violation of permit condition by owner of tractor-trailer was also alleged.
Based on pleadings, tribunal framed issues and recorded evidence of claimant no.1 as PW.1 and eyewitness as PW.2 and got marked Exs.P.1 to P.6.

Insurer examined its official as RW.1 and got marked Exs.R.1 and R.2.
5.
On consideration, tribunal has held accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver of tractor-trailer and held claimants were entitled for compensation.
It assessed by it at `9,71,400/-.

However on ground that Ex.R1-charge-sheet produced by insurer would indicate that driver of tractor-trailer was charge- sheeted for offence punishable under Sections 3, 181 and 187 of Motor Vehicles Act i.e., for driving vehicle without possessing valid and effective driving licence, it discharged liability of insurer and passed award against owner.

6. It was submitted that said conclusion was contrary to ratio laid down by this Court in case of IFFCO- NC: 2023:KHC-K:7369 TOKIO General Insurance Co. Ltd., vs. K. Prabhakar Reddy and Anr. (MFA no.865/2011 - 19.09.2013), that based only on charge-sheet, there cannot be presumption about non-possession of driving licence.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Even Apex Court in case of Rajesh Yadav vs. State of U.P1 has held that charge-sheet is opinion of investigating officer and therefore finding of tribunal called for interference.

7. Insofar as enhancement, it was submitted that deceased was 41 years of age, earning `10,000/-
per month as Mason, tribunal considered his monthly income at `4,000/- and by granting meager compensation under other heads was inadequate and sought enhancement.
8. On other hand, Shri Manvendra Reddy, learned counsel for respondent no.2/insurer sought to justify award.
It was submitted that insurer had in fact filed application to summon driver of insured vehicle to establish lack of driving licence, however said application was rejected.

It was also submitted that while assessing (2022) 12 SCC 200 NC: 2023:KHC-K:7369 compensation, though Smt.Sulabi And Ors vs Baswaraj And Anr on 13 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164632352/
3 deceased was more than 40 years of age, tribunal added 50% towards future prospects and said aspect would easily off-set any possibility for enhancement.
9.

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for parties.

Perused impugned judgment and award.
10. From above submission and since only claimants are in appeal challenging finding of tribunal regarding liability of insurer and for enhancement of compensation, points that would arise for consideration are :
"1) Whether dismissal of claim petition against insurer is justified ?
2) Whether claimants are entitled for enhancement of compensation?"
Point no.1 :
11.

To establish actionable negligence against insurer, claimants relied on FIR, Complaint, Spot Mahazar, Inquest Mahazar, Post Mortem Report and Motor Vehicle NC: 2023:KHC-K:7369 Inspectors Report marked as Exs.P.1 to P.6.
Ex.P.1 - FIR is registered based on Ex.P.2 - complaint.
Same impute negligence against driver of tractor.
Ex.R1 charge-sheet filed against tractor-trailer driver.
Though same would reveal that driver of tractor was charge-sheeted for offence punishable under Sections 181(3) and 187 of M.V.Act apart from offences under Indian Penal Code.
In view of decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in case of Rajesh Yadav (supra), charge-sheet would be collective opinion of investigating agency and cannot constitute evidence.
Hence, finding of tribunal based only on charge-sheet would be contrary to law and call for interference.
12. Indeed insurer has contended that it had issued notice to insured calling upon him to produce driving licence and etc. of the driver.
However, a specific finding is recorded by tribunal that no effort was made to place them on record.
Therefore, said contention would not hold water.
Consequently finding of tribunal dismissing claim petition would be unsustainable.
It is held that insurer NC: 2023:KHC-K:7369 would be liable to pay compensation.
Point no.1 is required to be answered in negative.

Point no.2 :
13.
Though claimants stated that Waman was 30 years of age, working as mason and earning `10,000/-, same was not substantiated with any specific evidence.
In absence, same has to be assessed notionally.
Notional income for year 2010 would be `5,500/-.
Therefore, tribunal would not be justified in taking it at `4,000/-.
Claimants are wife, four children and aged parents of deceased i.e., 7 in number.
Based on age mentioned in records, tribunal determined age of deceased as 41 years.
Deceased was self employed.

As per ratio laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court in case of National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi and others2, claimants would be entitled for addition of only 25% towards future prospects, deduction towards personal expenses will have to be at 1/5th and multiplier applicable (2017) 16 SCC 680 NC: 2023:KHC-K:7369 would be '14'.

sentences.text: Apart from above, claimant no.1/wife would be entitled for loss of 'spousal consortium' of `40,000/-; claimants no.2 to 5 - children loss of 'filial consortium' at `40,000/- each, claimants no.6 and 7 being parents of deceased entitled for loss of 'parental consortium' at `40,000/- each following ratio in Magma General Insurance Company Limited vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram and others3.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In addition, they would be entitled for `15,000/- towards 'funeral expenses' and `15,000/- towards 'loss of estate'.
15.
Since more than three years have lapsed after decision in Pranay Sethi's case (supra), they would be entitled for addition of 10% (`31,000/-) to award under conventional heads.
Thus, they would be entitled to total (2018) 18 SCC 130 - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:7369 compensation of `12,65,000/-.
Point no.2 is answered partly in affirmative.

Consequently, following :
ORDER (i) Appeal is allowed in part.

(ii) Claimants are entitled for total compensation of `12,65,000/- as against `9,71,400/-
awarded by tribunal with interest at 6% per annum from date of claim petition till deposit excluding period of 636 days being delay in filing appeal.
(iii) Direction issued by tribunal regarding  apportionment, deposit and release shall  apply to enhanced compensation  proportionately.

opennyai_summary.decision:
As per ratio laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court in case of National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi and others2, claimants would be entitled for addition of only 25% towards future prospects, deduction towards personal expenses will have to be at 1/5th and multiplier applicable (2017) 16 SCC 680 NC: 2023:KHC-K:7369 would be '14'.
4 `5500 + 25% X 4/5 X 12 X 14 = `9,24,000/-.
14.
Apart from above, claimant no.1/wife would be entitled for loss of 'spousal consortium' of `40,000/-; claimants no.2 to 5 - children loss of 'filial consortium' at `40,000/- each, claimants no.6 and 7 being parents of deceased entitled for loss of 'parental consortium' at `40,000/- each following ratio in Magma General Insurance Company Limited vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram and others3.
In addition, they would be entitled for `15,000/- towards 'funeral expenses' and `15,000/- towards 'loss of estate'.
15.
Since more than three years have lapsed after decision in Pranay Sethi's case (supra), they would be entitled for addition of 10% (`31,000/-) to award under conventional heads.
Thus, they would be entitled to total (2018) 18 SCC 130 - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:7369 compensation of `12,65,000/-.

awarded by tribunal with interest at 6% per annum from date of claim petition till deposit excluding period of 636 days being delay in filing appeal.
(iii) Direction issued by tribunal regarding  apportionment, deposit and release shall  apply to enhanced compensation  proportionately.
